format: Follows CPC 2010 ss.123–124 (in force from 15/9/2026): the charge states the offence (by name where the law gives one), the provision it is punishable under, and details of time, place and the person or thing involved.
disclaimer: Drafting guide only. Not the prescribed form. Check the wording against the evidence and the current Act before use.

templates.title: Murder — s.300(a), intention to cause death

fields.label: Deceased (name and ID)
fields.placeholder: Lim Ah Seng, NRIC No. S7654321B

fields.label: Act causing death (to wit)
fields.placeholder: stabbing him multiple times with a knife

templates.particulars: did commit murder by causing the death of one {victim}, to wit, by {act}, with the intention of causing death
notes: s.302(1) is for murder within s.300(a) (intention to cause death) and carries the mandatory death penalty. For s.300(b)–(d), use s.302(2).
Murder is a named offence, so it may be charged by that name (CPC s.123(2), illustration (c)).

templates.title: Murder — s.300(b), (c) or (d)

fields.label: Deceased (name and ID)
fields.placeholder: Lim Ah Seng, NRIC No. S7654321B

fields.label: Act causing death (to wit)
fields.placeholder: striking his head with a metal pipe

fields.label: Limb of s.300
options: with the intention of causing such bodily injury as you knew to be likely to cause death (s.300(b))
with the intention of causing bodily injury which was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death (s.300(c))
with knowledge that the act was so imminently dangerous that it must in all probability cause death or such bodily injury as is likely to cause death (s.300(d))

templates.particulars: did commit murder by causing the death of one {victim}, to wit, by {act}, {limb}
notes: Punishment: death or imprisonment for life, and if not punished with death, also liable to caning.

templates.title: Theft

fields.label: Property
fields.placeholder: one black iPhone 15 mobile phone

fields.label: In the possession of
fields.placeholder: Tan Ah Kow, NRIC No. S1234567A

templates.particulars: did commit theft of {property}, valued at about S${value}, in the possession of one {victim}
notes: Theft is a named offence (CPC s.123 illustration (c)). Max: 3 years, or fine, or both.
For a motor vehicle or a component part, use s.379A.

templates.title: Dishonest misappropriation of property

fields.label: Property
fields.placeholder: one black iPhone 15 mobile phone

fields.label: Belonging to
fields.placeholder: Tan Ah Kow, NRIC No. S1234567A

templates.particulars: did dishonestly misappropriate to your own use {property}, valued at about S${value}, belonging to one {victim}
notes: Statutory words: "dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use movable property". Max: 2 years, or fine, or both.
For s.403 a charge may state the gross sum and a date range of up to 12 months without listing each item or exact date, and is deemed one offence (CPC s.124(2)–(3)). Use the date-range option.

templates.title: Voluntarily causing hurt

fields.label: Victim (name and ID)
fields.placeholder: Tan Ah Kow, NRIC No. S1234567A

fields.label: Act done (to wit)
fields.placeholder: punching him on the face

templates.particulars: did voluntarily cause hurt to one {victim}, to wit, by {act}
notes: Max: 3 years, or fine up to $5,000, or both. Not for cases under s.323A (grievous hurt caused) or s.334 (grave and sudden provocation).

templates.title: Voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means

fields.label: Victim (name and ID)
fields.placeholder: Tan Ah Kow, NRIC No. S1234567A

fields.label: Weapon or means
fields.placeholder: a knife, an instrument for cutting

fields.label: Act done (to wit)
fields.placeholder: punching him on the face

templates.particulars: did voluntarily cause hurt to one {victim} by means of {means}, to wit, by {act}
notes: s.324 covers instruments for shooting, stabbing or cutting, instruments likely to cause death if used as a weapon, fire or heated substances, poison, corrosive or explosive substances, harmful substances, and animals. Max: 7 years, or fine, or caning, or any combination.

templates.title: Assault or criminal force to outrage modesty

fields.label: Victim (name and ID)
fields.placeholder: Tan Ah Kow, NRIC No. S1234567A

fields.label: Act done (to wit)
fields.placeholder: touching her buttocks with your hand

templates.particulars: did {force} one {victim}, to wit, by {act}, intending to outrage the modesty of the said {victim}
notes: Statutory mental element: "intending to outrage or knowing it to be likely that he will thereby outrage the modesty". Pick the limb that fits the evidence.
Victim below 14 years of age: use s.354(2) (max 5 years).

templates.title: Receiving or retaining stolen property

fields.label: Property
fields.placeholder: one black iPhone 15 mobile phone

fields.label: Property obtained through
options: property obtained in whole or in part through an offence involving fraud or dishonesty

templates.particulars: did {mode} {property}, valued at about S${value}, knowing or having reason to believe the same to be {origin}
notes: Statutory words: "receives or retains any property, knowing or having reason to believe the property to be stolen property or property obtained in whole or in part through an offence involving fraud or dishonesty". Max: 5 years, or fine, or both.
Gross sum and date range allowed (CPC s.124(3)(a)).

templates.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property

fields.label: Victim (name and ID)
fields.placeholder: Tan Ah Kow, NRIC No. S1234567A

fields.label: Deception ("into believing that ...")
fields.placeholder: you would deliver a Rolex watch to her upon payment

fields.label: Property delivered
fields.placeholder: S$3,500 in cash

fields.label: Delivered to
fields.placeholder: you

templates.particulars: did cheat one {victim}, by deceiving the said {victim} into believing that {deception}, and by such manner of deception you dishonestly induced the said {victim} to deliver {property} to {recipient}
notes: Cheating is a named offence (CPC s.123 illustration (c)). Max: 10 years, and liable to fine or caning or both.
If the cheating was by remote communication, check s.420(2).

templates.title: Criminal intimidation

fields.label: Victim (name and ID)
fields.placeholder: Tan Ah Kow, NRIC No. S1234567A

fields.label: Threat (to wit)
fields.placeholder: saying to him "I will kill you"

fields.label: Intent
options: to cause alarm to the said {victim}
to cause the said {victim} to do an act which the said {victim} was not legally bound to do
to cause the said {victim} to omit to do an act which the said {victim} was legally entitled to do

templates.particulars: did commit criminal intimidation by threatening one {victim} with injury to {injury} of the said {victim}, to wit, by {threat}, with intent {intent}
notes: Criminal intimidation is a named offence (CPC s.123 illustration (c)). Max: 2 years, or fine, or both. If the threat is to cause death or grievous hurt, destruction of property by fire, or an offence punishable with death or 7 years or more: max 10 years.
Check the s.503 definition for threats to a person in whom the victim is interested.
